segments.he: גְּמָ׳ הָא אִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁירָה לָהּ — אַף הֵן כְּשֵׁירִין לָהּ. אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת, גַּזְלָן דְּדִבְרֵיהֶם כְּשֵׁירִין לְעֵדוּת אִשָּׁה.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «This» implies that any testimony «for which a woman is fit, these too are fit. Rav Ashi said: That is to say,» one who is regarded as «a robber by rabbinic law,» i.e., one who illegally came into possession of money but did not actually steal it from another, is like those mentioned in the mishna. Although they are generally unfit to give testimony, «they are fit» to give «testimony» to enable «a woman» to remarry.

moves.summary: the mishna implies: where a woman is fit, these are fit
moves.about: the mishna's rule implies its converse: testimony a woman is fit for, these too are fit for

moves.summary: hence a rabbinic-law robber is fit to testify for a woman
